title: Theo Thinks His Tax Refund Is a Bonus 😂
description:
Theo just got a $3,273 tax refund and he's calling it a bonus from the IRS. Nora breaks the news: it's his own money. He had too much tax taken out of his pay all year, and the IRS is simply handing it back. Spread over 12 months, that's about $273 a month he lent the government, at 0% interest.

A big refund feels like a win, but it usually means smaller paychecks all year. Updating your W-4 changes how much is withheld, so more lands in each paycheck (and the refund shrinks). Withhold too little and you could owe instead, so aim close to the right amount.

Did you get a refund or owe this year? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Assumptions: $3,273 is the average US individual refund in the 2026 filing season (IRS Filing Season Statistics, cumulative to 1 May 2026). The video assumes all of Theo's refund came from over-withholding; many real refunds also include refundable credits. $273/month = $3,273 ÷ 12. Illustration only. This is not financial advice.
